# Installer

<!-- Generated by go run ./tools/releaseartifacts -write-doc. Do not edit by hand. -->

[Back to Release Artifacts](../release-artifacts.md)

macOS/Linux users can install the latest release with:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teamswyg/riido-daemon/main/scripts/install-riido-daemon.sh | sh
```

The installer script:

- detects `darwin`, `linux` and `amd64`, `arm64`
- resolves latest through the GitHub Releases API so prerelease tags are installable
- downloads the matching release asset and `SHA256SUMS`
- verifies the checksum before installation
- installs `riido` to `$HOME/.riido/bin` unless `RIIDO_DAEMON_INSTALL_DIR` is set
- installs the adjacent `VERSION`, and on macOS the signed `RiidoCLIAuthHelper.app` with `CLI_AUTH_HELPER.json`; a package without the helper removes an older helper, and a package with only one of the pair is rejected before the existing binary is touched
- prints the PATH line for the current shell, or warns when another `riido` is found first on PATH

Use a specific version with:

```bash
RIIDO_DAEMON_VERSION=v0.0.1 \
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teamswyg/riido-daemon/main/scripts/install-riido-daemon.sh | sh
```

Install the package the desktop app uses for a channel (`staging`, `latest`) from the CDN with:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teamswyg/riido-daemon/main/scripts/install-riido-daemon.sh | RIIDO_DAEMON_CHANNEL=staging sh
```

- Channels read the active CDN feeds the desktop app uses: `latest` reads `releases/safe/ai-agent` and `staging` reads `releases/staging-safe/ai-agent`. The legacy `releases/latest` and `releases/staging` prefixes stay frozen.
- Production stays `riido` in `$HOME/.riido/bin` (no channel, or `latest`); such an install removes a staging `INSTALL_CHANNEL` marker left in that directory.
- `staging` is the test channel (RIID-6036): the same package installs to `$HOME/.riido-staging/libexec` with an `INSTALL_CHANNEL` marker, and only the `riido-staging` link in `$HOME/.riido-staging/bin` (`RIIDO_DAEMON_LINK_DIR`) goes on PATH, so it never replaces production `riido`. The marker makes the binary default to the staging profile, keep its settings in `riido-cli-staging`, and update from the staging feed.
